  answer. A closed gutter is pointer-events: none — so the tap falls through to the cell — which is the finger's version
  of "hovering blank gutter still reveals the icons" that gutter.css already documents for a pointer. The reader who prods
  the empty column gets the controls.

  I found that by catching a defect in the new test: it asserted that tapping a closed gutter does not select, and passed
  — but only because jsdom doesn't implement pointer-events. A green assertion about a state a browser cannot produce.
  Rewritten against the open "…" panel, which takes its hit-testing back on purpose (it's opaque, and the paragraph behind
  it mustn't be pressable through it) and so is the state the exclusion entry actually defends. Mutating the entry away
  now makes it red.

  The full suite is still running in tmux with no failures so far; the box refused a couple of new vitest starts on memory
  pressure, which is the admission guard, not a test result.
